records.title: Spectral FFT ocean

urls.readDepth: author text verbatim from og:description
rendered README on the repository page read for the technique list, plus API commit and tree at the pin, plus the whole implementation file

records.methodExtracted: 3 cascades at 768/121/19 m partitioning k-space without overlap; 512^2 inverse FFT per cascade per frame as a Cooley-Tukey butterfly with a precomputed twiddle/index texture, two MRT slots carrying four complex fields through one butterfly; JONSWAP with TMA shallow-water correction and Donelan-Banner spreading, driven by real wind speed, fetch and depth; Tessendorf h0 = (xi_r + i*xi_i)*sqrt(P); h(k,t) from h0(k) and conj(h0(-k)); foam injected where the Jacobian of the Tessendorf displacement goes negative, then accumulated temporally.
records.compatibilityDifferences: Ours is one cascade at N=32 on the CPU in JavaScript, a plain iterative radix-2 transform instead of a butterfly texture and MRT, cos^2s spreading instead of Donelan-Banner, and a per-frame Jacobian foam test with no temporal accumulation. Upstream is WebGL2 + GLSL; this repository forbids ShaderMaterial/GLSL, so the surface is core materials with vertex colours.
records.cpuCheck: as above, plus an explicit assertion that the displacement Jacobian drops below 1 (a summed-sine surface never folds) and that gridN is 32
